terms.definition: The point-of-care system carries out the health worker's decisions on decision-support guidance: each accepted action's request becomes active (intent plan or order) and joins the client's CarePlan; a declined action is not written. Input is the guidance and the decisions; output is the transaction Bundle saved.

The point-of-care system applies a DAK decision table's PlanDefinition to one client ($apply) and gets the proposed actions back as a RequestGroup (R4; RequestOrchestration in R5), or as CDS Hooks cards when the guidance comes from a CDS service. Input is the PlanDefinition and the client; output is the proposal, every request in it still a proposal.

Classify and code L1 narrative content (recommendations, implementation practices, remarks, and proposed coverage exclusions) and L2 DAK slots (personas, business processes, guideline domains, conditions, interventions, medicines, and GRADE ratings) using the `terminology-coding` methodology and the `terminology-lookup` Tool. Covers the authoring-agent's four-rung reuse-first lookup, the `l1-extraction-reviewer` lane that reads and signs proposed L1 coverage exclusions against the printed page, and the `terminologist` / ontologist lane that adjudicates candidate codings and local glossary candidates.

A health worker (or a client, on their own device) completes a FHIR R4 Questionnaire conforming to Structured Data Capture as their device renders it, and the result is a QuestionnaireResponse. Generic for any DAK form: a registration, a visit, a referral. Input is the Questionnaire as rendered, with any pre-populated answers; output is the completed QuestionnaireResponse.

Build a DAK's library from the L1 sources its Component 1 cites, and the L1 knowledge graph that records them. Read when starting or extending a DAK library, when a DAK's guidance changes, and before writing any L1 graph for a DAK. Covers fetching a cited WHO IRIS item, ingesting it, deciding whether it is L1 (declared > context > inferred), extracting the Component 1 graph, the L1 graph of each L1 source as a specialisation of its library entry, and the layering rule: the library is upstream of L1.

What the DAK post-processing phase produces after the IG Publisher runs — the JSON/JSON-LD surface, the DAK API hub, and the metadata-to-Liquid bridge — and how an IG repository's own site gets the same sidecars from the cached AST (`ig-site:sidecars`). Read before changing a post-processing step, and before assuming the Publisher produced something it did not.

What each DAK pre-processing step does before the IG Publisher runs, which steps exist only to feed the Publisher's page index, and how the phase runs as the overlay on fhir-harness's AST cache refresh (`dak-pre-export.sh`). Also which files in a DAK repository are authored and which are generated, and the SEMVER rule for DAK and IG versions. Read before changing, assuming or moving a pre-processing step.

How a WHO Digital Transformation Handbook (DTH) is produced, from sources to publication, in the seven stages and milestones of dth-authoring.bpmn — and the rules the diagram cannot carry: which review sheet each stage uses, the DAK kinds every DTH is written in, and how a term is deprecated. Read before starting a new DTH, before moving one to its next stage, and before setting up its feedback or public-comment sheet.

Turn a WHO Digital Transformation Handbook that exists only as an L1 publication (ingested in who-iris) into an L2 DTH in its own repository that depends on smart-ra: write the handbook's workplan first (what goes in its repo, what goes in smart-ra, which BPMN, roles and DMN to model), then scaffold and seed it. Read before starting work on any dth-* handbook repo.

The point-of-care system turns a completed QuestionnaireResponse into the FHIR resources it stands for, by the extraction its SDC Questionnaire declares (StructureMap-based, definition-based or observation-based $extract), and saves them. Input is the response and its Questionnaire; output is a transaction Bundle. Generic for any DAK form.

GRADE — the grading system a WHO guideline folio declares for certainty of evidence, and the Evidence-to-Decision judgement a recommendation rests on. Read when a folio's `Task_AppraiseGrade` runs under GRADE, before recording a certainty, an EtD judgement or a recommendation's direction and strength.

Stage 0 of smart-guideline-end-to-end: turn a request for a SMART Guideline into a use case — population, setting, jurisdiction and interventions in scope, new or an adaptation — in the requester's own words. The agent asks numbered questions for what the request did not say, and never invents the answer. Read when a guideline request arrives, before any L1 source is looked for.

Extract the indicators an L1 source prints (indicator reference or metadata sheets: name, numerator, denominator, disaggregation, definition, data sources) as L1 `indicator` nodes with every printed field, then draft one L2 program indicator per indicator, derived from its L1 node. Read before adding a WHO handbook's or guideline's indicators to a DAK or a DTH, and whenever an L2 indicator has to trace to its source. Part of L1 → L2 extraction for every DAK and DTH, beside recommendation-extraction.

A health worker tells the client (or caregiver) what was decided and what happens next, in words and, where the DAK gives one, on a slip or card: a referral, a return date, a result. Input is what to tell and the client's language; output is that the client was told, and what they were handed. Generic for any DAK step that ends with the client being informed.

How one L2 DAK component is edited by the agent and reviewed by a person: personas and user scenarios, BPMN business processes, DMN decision and scheduling logic, core data elements and glossary with their terminology bindings, indicators and requirements. One subprocess for all of them. The agent edits, checks, renders and stages with a before/after, then hands the component on, and review forks alongside it without blocking. Per component, it lists the authoring skill, checker, renderer and diff, reviewing role, and what the reviewer judges. Read before authoring or reviewing any L2 component, and when an L2 track asks what its reviewer needs to see.

Author the L2 layer of a WHO SMART Guideline — the Digital Adaptation Kit between the narrative L1 guideline and the L3 FHIR artefacts — one DAK component per pass (personas, user scenarios, business processes, data dictionary, decision and scheduling logic, indicators, requirements), each edited and then reviewed alongside through l2-component-edit-review. Stage 4 of smart-guideline-end-to-end and the authoring steps of l2-dak-authoring.bpmn. Read before authoring or adapting any DAK component.

Stage 3 of smart-guideline-end-to-end: choose which existing DAKs (WHO's, or a jurisdiction's adaptation) the guideline builds on. From the L1 knowledge graph and any known candidates, one decision row per candidate DAK — reuse, adapt, extend or reject, with evidence and a reason — laid out as a decision-comparison table and put to the adjudicators as a DecisionRequest. Also defines the dependency decision row that stage 5 (l3-dependency-choice) uses at L3. Read before choosing, or recording, a DAK dependency.

Stage 5 of smart-guideline-end-to-end: choose which existing FHIR IGs (WHO's, or a jurisdiction's) the guideline's L3 builds on. Indexes each candidate IG with ig-artifact-ingestion, matches the L1 knowledge graph and the stage-4 L2 assets against the index, and returns one decision row per IG naming the profiles, value sets and libraries reused, derived from or not used. Read before choosing, or recording, an IG dependency.

The check between stages 5 and 6 of smart-guideline-end-to-end (Gateway_L3Ready): may the agent write L3 assets yet? Yes only when every source of the use case has its L1 extraction, every L2 asset names the L1 node it rests on, every L3 artefact about to be written names the L2 asset it implements, and the review of each extraction and L2 asset has been requested. Returns the answer, every finding with the stage that fixes it, and what was checked. Read before writing any FSH, CQL or other L3 file for a guideline or an adaptation.

Stage 7 of smart-guideline-end-to-end: get from the requester a description of the consuming application — who uses it, on what device, which L2 processes and L3 resources it covers, connectivity, the systems it talks to — and turn it into the design intent wireframe-design-review starts from. The agent offers options drawn from the L2 personas and processes, and never invents the application. Read before wireframing or building an L4 application on a guideline.

Stage 8b of smart-guideline-end-to-end: build the consuming application against the stage-6 IG build (a clean build, not a publication), from the brief and the chosen stage-8a wireframes, with conformance tests from the IG's examples and test cases and a walk through each L2 user scenario it serves. Read before building an L4 application on a guideline.

Run an L4 application that is already built, on the agent's own machine, against a clean IG build, so a person can try or demonstrate it before anything is hosted. Read before starting a local copy of an L4 app for a review, a demo or a country adaptation check.

Turn one ingested L1 source into L1 3.0 recommendation nodes: list every normative sentence as a candidate, let the agent decide each in a curation file, then refuse a non-verbatim statement or unknown location and write the graph, coverage and proposed exclusions. Step 1 of recommendation-extraction, run once per included source; the `l1-recommendation-candidates` Tool satisfies it.

Extract the recommendations of an L1 source as L1 3.0 recommendation and remark nodes, then describe each one's scenario: the persona (role) who acts on it, the business process they act in, and the user story, as smart-kg L2 user-scenario candidates that reuse the target guide's own vocabulary. Read before extracting recommendations from a WHO guideline or position paper with no printed "Recommendation N" labels, before linking a recommendation to a DAK persona or process, and whenever a recommendation has to say who does it and where. Covers the hybrid extraction (mechanical candidates, agent structuring, verbatim and 100 % coverage gates), the reuse-first precedence for personas and processes, the WARNING format, and sign-off.

Join each L1 recommendation to who acts on it and during which business process: one smart-kg L2 user-scenario candidate per recommendation, from the agent's mapping, reusing the target guide's personas and processes first, then smart-base's generic personas, and never inventing a process. Step 2 of recommendation-extraction; the `l1-recommendation-scenarios` Tool satisfies it.

OPTIONAL and never blocking: a health worker who chooses to may note why they accepted or declined decision-support guidance, in one tap plus an optional coded or free-text reason. Input is the decision; output is one FHIR Provenance (or nothing, when skipped, which is the default). The care plan is updated whether or not this is ever done.

A health worker reads the client's history as their device shows it (an International Patient Summary, imported records, or a paper card and what the client reports) and takes into account what bears on today's care, weighing each item by where it came from: verified, unverified or reported. Input is the records with their provenance; output is what the health worker relies on.

A health worker sees the decision-support guidance for one client on their device (the proposed actions of a RequestGroup or CDS Hooks cards) and accepts or declines each action; modifies one only where the device offers it. Input is the guidance as rendered; output is the decision per action. At most one tap per action; nothing else is asked.

Somebody asked for a new WHO SMART Guideline (an IG built on smart-base, or a DAK that will feed one). Specialises fhir-ig-create: the same three facts, the same numbered question with the same default (stage it inside this repository first), and the same routes, plus the SMART rules: every guideline repository instantiates smart-base identically, forks under litlfred come before any WHO repository, the identity comes from the declaration and never from the directory, and the WHO template's theme and chrome come from smart-base by `needs`, never copied. Use whenever a user asks to create, start or set up a SMART Guideline, a SMART IG, a WHO IG or a DAK.

The whole road from a use case to a running application on WHO SMART Guidelines, for a new guideline or a jurisdiction's adaptation, as an orchestrator of ten named stage skills, each with its own input and output contract: guideline-use-case, dak-l1-library, recommendation-extraction, l2-dependency-choice, l2-dak-authoring, l3-dependency-choice, l3-fhir-authoring, l4-application-brief, wireframe-design-review and l4-application-build. Each stage's output is the next stage's input. Human adjudication follows every stage as QA, not as a gate, but the order of the stages is a rule: no L3 asset before the L1 extraction and L2 assets it derives from exist with their review requested. Read before starting any end-to-end authoring or adaptation, and to find which skill runs each stage. A request to adapt a WHO guideline, DAK or IG to a country or programme ("adapt the immunization guidelines to Uganda using these schedules") is this process, even when it reads like an IG or coding task.

Which layer a WHO SMART asset, rule, script or page belongs to — fhir-harness, smart-base (with its L1 and DAK document kinds) or smart-ig — and the one question that settles it. Read before adding anything to fhir-harness, smart-base or smart-ig, before creating a per-IG harness, and before moving a pre/post-processing step.

Taking ownership of the WHO smart-base scripts in litlfred, rewriting them to the Skill I/O contract, and the one gate that governs when a script may actually move. Read before touching, copying or rewriting any upstream smart-base script.

Check L1 authored from pictures (a schedule poster, a slide deck: a source with no usable text layer) against the image narratives and transcriptions it names: every statement verbatim in one of them, every transcription word corroborated by the entry's text layer unless listed under inspectionOnly, and unique keys. A step of recommendation-extraction, in place of recommendation-candidates when that step found no normative sentence; the `l1-transcription-verbatim` Tool satisfies it.
